title: Uniform integrability of truncated continuum-polymer partition functions for positive-jump Lévy noise with finite large-jump first moment and dimension-dependent small-jump moments
source_title: The continuum directed polymer in Lévy noise
author: Quentin Berger; Hubert Lacoin
difficulty_reason: Standard positive-martingale convergence does not provide L1 convergence when the unrestricted second moment can diverge. The authors construct good-trajectory truncations and control intersecting Poisson replicas by stochastic comparisons and dimension-dependent multibody energy constraints. The resulting summable simplex bounds make the truncation error uniformly small and close uniform integrability in every printed dimension case.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Independent Proposition4.1 for finite positive beta and time horizon, Poisson intensity dt dx lambda(du) on positive jumps, lambda([a,infinity)) finite for all a>0, integral over[1,infinity) of u lambda(du) finite, and exact2.10: finite small-jump second moment in dimension1, or finite small-jump p moment for some p<1+2/d in dimensions at least2. Gives almost-sure and L1 convergence of the unnormalized partition function via uniform integrability, without a separate positivity/tightness or discrete-scaling-limit claim. All new replica decomposition, multibody restriction, first/second moment bounds and AppendixC stochastic comparisons read; AppendixB.1 positivity representation and martingale proof included. Mecke formula, Gaussian convolution, Dirichlet simplex integrals and standard martingale convergence are explicit existing foundations. The final gamma-function signs on42 are swapped relative to the explicit simplex integrand4.32 and the chosen integrability inequality directly preceding it; bounded standard integral evaluation suffices with the supplied construction, no new stochastic estimate. Replica beta powers and harmless finite exponential constants are compressed in intermediate displays; only uniform finiteness is selected, not a quantitative numerical bound. No criterion for infinite large-jump mean, positive limiting Gibbs measure, singular-path description, point-to-point parameter variant or sharp necessary threshold separately counted.
